class: An exception audit that bans one spelling of silence while the same silence spreads in other spellings, plus 268 copies of one truncation idiom
fix: diagnostics.short_exc (bounded first line; type name on empty messages instead of IndexError) replaces all inline copies; diagnostics.probe marks deliberately silent probes (first use: _process_alive); tests/test_no_silent_handlers.py ratchets every file at its current silent-handler count so no new handler may be added without logging, raising, or @probe.
prevention: Audits state the property (a handler leaves a trace), not the spelling; shared idioms get one helper before the count spreads.
root_cause: test_no_silent_swallow only flagged single-statement `pass` bodies, so silence moved into `except: continue`, `except: return False` and bare fallbacks (400 handlers tree-wide), while str(exc).splitlines()[0][:100] was copied to 268 sites -- where it raises IndexError on empty messages.
symptom: Runs stalled without saying why (silence in new spellings), and error logging itself could crash on empty exception messages.
why_tests_missed: The audit matched syntax (`pass`) instead of the property (leaves a trace), and no test covered the truncation idiom's empty-message case.
